articles.title: Gaethje’s Next Fight Is Already Decided #ufc
articles.description: Justin Gaethje says he doesn’t want rematches — but Chael Sonnen explains why he may have no choice when it comes to Ilia Topuria. Despite Gaethje’s reluctance to fight the same opponent twice, Chael argues that Ilia is clearly the No. 1 contender and shouldn’t be punished for losing a razor-close, brutal fight. After going deep into exhaustion against Gaethje, Ilia’s return could have been the perfect opportunity to demand the rematch — but instead, Gaethje may be the one facing the decision. What happens if Gaethje refuses? Could Kamaru Usman enter the picture? Would Gaethje demand an immediate rematch clause before agreeing to fight Ilia again? Chael breaks down why the UFC may ultimately force Gaethje’s hand — and why there may be nowhere left for him to go except back into the fire with Topuria. #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #UFCLightweight #MMA

articles.title: This Is Why I Love Wrestling
articles.description: Sometimes in wrestling, you only need one good day. Chael Sonnen tells the story of Blaine Natal, a wrestler he's known and coached for years. Blaine has spent his life showing up, taking the hard matches and refusing to let failure determine whether he steps on the mat again. His mother, Candy, has been there for all of it. But for all the years of work, Blaine was still waiting for that day. Then he drew Noah Wachsmuth, an undefeated Oregon champion and former Olympic Training Center athlete. On paper, this wasn't supposed to be Blaine's moment. For much of the match, it didn't look like it would be. But wrestling doesn't reward how impressive something looks. The scoreboard does the talking. When time expired, Blaine had one more point. After 22 years, he finally had his day. For Chael, it was one of those rare moments in sports that brought a tear to his eye. You don't need 10 years of perfect days. Sometimes you just need one. articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Chael Sonnen isn't convinced. By every normal measure, Volkanovski should be declining. He's been through wars, suffered losses, made his money and reached an age where most fighters don't regain the top spot once it's taken from them. Except Volk already did exactly that. Chael looks at what makes Volkanovski different, the way he chooses opponents, why he consistently asks for the toughest available challenger, and the question that could define the end of his career. Does Volk eventually decide for himself that it's time to walk away? Or is the kind of competitor who keeps going until somebody forces him to stop? Because even if Volkanovski's best days really are behind him, his diminished version might still be better than almost everybody else. articles.title: Why Topuria DESERVES the Gaethje Rematch
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #dkpartner The reaction to a possible Ilia Topuria vs Justin Gaethje rematch has surprised Chael Sonnen. A lot of fans aren't simply saying they'd rather see another matchup. They're arguing that there is no competitive reason to run this fight back. Chael couldn't disagree more. Topuria hurt Gaethje badly, pushed for the finish, and ultimately faded as the fight went long. Sean O'Malley even pointed out a moment where Topuria may have been able to secure a TKO had he walked away after dropping Gaethje with a body shot. Then look at Topuria's résumé. He was undefeated, a two-division UFC champion, stopped Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira, and entered the Gaethje fight after a long period of inactivity and major changes outside the cage. So why is a rematch suddenly unreasonable? Chael breaks down the competitive case for Topuria vs Gaethje 2, responds to Luke Thomas' argument, and explains why this fight may have far more justification than people are giving it credit for. Would you run Topuria vs Gaethje back, or should both men move on? articles.title: Is Tommy McMillen the UFC’s Next Superstar?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Could Tommy “Gun” McMillen become the second-biggest star in UFC history? Conor McGregor remains the standard, but determining who belongs directly behind him is more complicated. Georges St-Pierre produced enormous pay-per-view numbers. Paddy Pimblett has become a massive attraction. Ilia Topuria, Islam Makhachev, Sean O’Malley, Ronda Rousey and Jon Jones all have arguments depending on how stardom is measured. Chael Sonnen believes McMillen could eventually surpass nearly all of them. Tommy has the fighting ability, an authentic personality and the rare ability to deliver a promotional line without making it sound rehearsed. He also trains alongside O’Malley under Tim Welch, giving him access to people who understand that becoming a star requires more than winning fights. McMillen’s undefeated record survived another major test at Noche UFC when he defeated Marwan Rahiki by unanimous decision in a back-and-forth fight. Instead of exposing Tommy, the adversity allowed him to demonstrate toughness, composure and the ability to close strongly. There are still questions. Tommy must continue winning, reach numbered UFC events and discover what will motivate him once the money and attention arrive. But right now, Chael sees no evidence that disqualifies him from becoming the UFC’s next transcendent superstar. articles.title: Tom Aspinall Vacates UFC Heavyweight Title
articles.description: Tom Aspinall has officially vacated the UFC heavyweight championship after ongoing complications with his eyes prevented him from receiving medical clearance. Aspinall revealed that he had agreed to a fight date, returned to sparring and felt ready to compete. Then another accident caused further damage to his right eye. Rather than continue holding up the heavyweight division, Tom made the difficult decision to relinquish the title. Chael Sonnen reacts to Aspinall’s deeply personal statement and acknowledges that the MMA community, including Chael himself, did not understand how serious the situation had become. But Tom’s announcement also creates a major development that many headlines are overlooking. With Aspinall stepping aside, interim champion Ciryl Gane is positioned as the undisputed UFC heavyweight champion. The question now becomes who gets the first opportunity against him. Does Josh Hokit’s aggressive campaign earn him the fight? Could Alex Pereira receive another opportunity? Or will Alexander Volkov finally enter the conversation? Chael breaks down Tom’s decision, Ciryl Gane’s new position and the battle to become the UFC’s next heavyweight title challenger. articles.title: Ilia Topuria Wants Justin Gaethje, NOW!
articles.description: Ilia Topuria wants an immediate rematch with Justin Gaethje, and Chael Sonnen doesn't understand the resistance. Topuria was an undefeated champion and the favorite before Gaethje pulled off the upset. With the rest of the lightweight division still sorting itself out, Chael believes Topuria remains one of the most logical options for Gaethje's next title defense. Gaethje has publicly said he doesn't want rematches. He wants new names and new experiences before his career ends. But Chael doesn't believe that means Gaethje would actually turn Topuria down if the UFC made the call. Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy still have business to settle. Usman Nurmagomedov isn't in the UFC yet. Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira have their own complications. Start eliminating the alternatives, and Chael keeps coming back to the same name.
